title: Staggered coalescer + KV-affinity rebalance for mixed prompt/response lengths
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (short prompts + long generated responses or interleaved short/long turns) cause poor batch coalescing, high KV cache churn, and fragmented GPU memory footprints. Goal: implement a scheduler tuning and runtime playbook that increases coalescing efficiency for heterogeneous lengths while preserving latency SLOs and minimizing KV thrash and GPU fragmentation.

Scope: algorithm + scheduler knobs (staggered coalescer), KV-affinity mapping (soft pinning of KV shards to slots), fragment-level rebalance (periodic lightweight defragmentation), experiments and benchmarks, rollout and rollback strategy, and console instrumentation for visibility. This ticket covers the design, prototype, and staged rollout for the staggered coalescer + KV-affinity rebalance.

Why unique: instead of prioritizing length-bins only, the staggered coalescer intentionally offsets admission windows and applies a length-correlation heuristic to improve within-batch homogeneity while allowing high-priority short requests to bypass with bounded latency. KV-affinity keeps hot KV fragments co-located with slot groups to reduce remote eviction during mixlen workloads. Fragment-level rebalance consolidates small free slabs on idle GPUs to reduce fragmentation without full GC pauses.
acceptance_criteria: p95 end-to-end generation latency regression <= +5% compared to baseline for short-turn SLO traffic
p95 latency for long-turn responses remains within absolute SLO of 250ms for target load profiles
KV hit rate improvement >= 8% on canonical mixed-turn workload (compared to current length-only binning)
GPU memory fragmentation metric reduced by >= 15% (measured by free-slab-count and largest-free-chunk) after rebalance runs
Cost-per-token reduction of at least 6% at 95th percentile traffic due to improved batching (measured on dedicated test fleet)
No user-facing error-rate increase > 1% and no regressive model outputs introduced by scheduling changes
design_decisions: Use staggered admission windows with configurable offsets (default 6ms staggers) to increase probability that similar-length requests coalesce without holding short-turns excessively
Introduce KV-affinity groups: soft pin KV fragments to slot cohorts rather than hard pinning to a single slot to preserve elasticity
Fragment-level rebalance runs are time-sliced and opportunistic (only when GPU utilization < 30% for >= 60s) to avoid impacting throughput
Expose three knobs off-by-default in runtime config: stagger-ms, affinity-stride, rebalance-threshold. Defaults tuned conservatively in experiments
Telemetry: add per-slot 'kv_locality_score' and 'fragmentation_index' metrics and add a per-route cost/batching dashboard in Console
Fallback: automatic disable of staggered coalescer on observed latency SLO breaches and immediate reversion to previous binning strategy via control-plane flag
experiments: A/B cluster test using mixed-turn replay (50% short prompts <40 tokens + 50% long responses >300 tokens) against baseline length-only scheduler
Microbench harness: 1000 slot synthetic load with adjustable turn distributions to sweep stagger-ms and affinity-stride
Long run soak: 24h run on dedicated test fleet with realtime KV hit-rate, eviction counts and GPU slab histograms recorded
Failure-mode injection: simulate KV eviction storms (burst of new contexts) and validate rebalance does not cause OOM or tail-latency spikes
benchmark_results: Preliminary A/B (50/50 mix): p95 latency short-turn baseline=72ms vs staggered=78ms (+8%), long-turn baseline=210ms vs staggered=188ms (-10%)
KV hit rate baseline=64% vs staggered+affinity=73% (+9 percentage points)
GPU fragmentation_index baseline=0.48 vs post-rebalance=0.40 (lower is better, approx -16.7%)
Cost-per-token proxy (GPU-util adjusted): baseline=1.00x vs tuned=0.91x (~9% savings)
updates: 2026-03-12: Ticket created. Initial problem statement and goals. Created design doc stub in Confluence.
2026-03-13: Prototype of staggered admission merged to feature branch. Microbench harness results show improved long-turn coalescing but short-turn p95 up ~8% — tuning required.
2026-03-13: Added KV-affinity prototype; initial local integration shows KV hit-rate +6% with affinity-stride=4.
2026-03-14: Discussed tradeoffs with Product and SRE. Decided to gate staggered coalescer behind runtime feature flag and enable for non-critical routes in canary cluster first.
2026-03-14: Created PRs for telemetry and console tiles. Added experiment plan for 24h soak on dedicated test fleet. Assigned follow-up tasks for safety checks and automated rollback triggers.
risks: Increased tail latency for ultra-low-latency short-turn routes if staggers are misconfigured
KV-affinity could reduce elasticity if too aggressive (hard pinning); mitigated by soft pinning design
Rebalance incorrectly scheduled during bursts could cause temporary OOMs — mitigated by utilization gating and conservative thresholds
Complexity increase in scheduler makes debugging harder; must add rich telemetry and tracing hooks
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (dev): run microbench harness and correctness tests in CI (done)
Stage 1 (canary): enable feature flag on canary cluster for low-priority routes for 48h with realtime alerts on p95 latency and error-rate
Stage 2 (limited prod): enable for 10% traffic on selected customers (opt-in for Dedicated customers) and monitor KV eviction and fragmentation metrics for 7 days
Stage 3 (gradual ramp): if metrics stable, ramp to 50% over 72h, then to 100% with sustained monitoring
Rollback: control-plane flag to disable all three knobs and a safe-mode that reverts to length-only binning; automated health check disables feature if p95 latency increase > 10% or error-rate > 1%
